# Proofing dough

Proofing is the final rise of shaped bread dough before baking. The yeast from the [[Sourdough levain]] fills the gluten network with gas so the loaf turns out light and open.

Proof the shaped loaf in the fridge overnight. The cold slows the yeast, deepens the sourdough flavour and makes the dough easier to score.

Press the dough with a floured finger. If the dent springs back slowly and only partly, the loaf is ready to bake in the [[Baking in a dutch oven|dutch oven]].
